narrative.title: The Two-Clamp Balance Check
narrative.scenario: A treasury terminal holds account balances in a sorted tree and must verify whether any two distinct accounts can settle an invoice exactly — their balances summing to the target. Instead of dumping the tree into a list, the terminal clamps from both ends simultaneously: the smallest candidate climbs up while the largest climbs down, adjusting whichever side overshoots until they meet or cross.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) and an integer k — the target sum.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if two distinct nodes hold values summing to k, otherwise false.

testCases.explanation: The pair 2 + 7 (or 3 + 6) hits the target exactly.
The two largest values 6 and 7 already sum to only 13.

hintLevels: Level 1: Flattening to an array works, but two live cursors can walk the sorted order without it.
Level 2: One stack feeds the next-smallest, another the next-largest — the classic two-pointer sweep on a stream.
Level 3: Sum too small advances the low cursor; too big retreats the high one; cursors crossing means no pair exists.
